body:
Same family, one more screen — measured while implementing #4570 (PR #4579). Commenting here rather than opening a twin, since the fix shape you describe ("move through the existing console bundle") is identical.

**The Settings namespace page (`apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsView.tsx`) routes zero framing copy through i18n.** Every user-visible string on it is a hardcoded English literal:

| string | where |
|---|---|
| `Settings saved` | success toast after a save |
| `Save failed` | generic failure toast |
| `Locked by environment: KEY` | the SETTINGS_LOCKED refusal toast |
| `Action failed` / `Action succeeded` | settings action buttons |
| `Failed to load settings` | load-error card fallback |
| `No namespace selected.` | empty-route state |
| `All settings` / `Back` | navigation buttons |
| `Discard` / `Save changes` | the unsaved-changes save bar |
| `N unsaved change(s)` | save-bar counter (also has an English-only plural rule) |

What makes it worth recording as one item rather than nine: **its immediate sibling already does the right thing.** `SettingsHub.tsx`, in the same directory, resolves through `t('console.settingsHub.*')` against the same bundle that ships all ten packs. So this is not a missing capability or an unwired screen — it is one file that was written against a different convention than the file next to it, which matches your framing of these as "omissions from an otherwise complete bundle".

Same "an app cannot work around it" property you note: `useSettingsLabel` resolves manifest-authored labels (title, description, field labels, option labels), so a plugin author can translate the *content* of a settings namespace but has no key that reaches the *chrome* around it. A zh-CN admin sees translated field labels sitting inside an English save bar.

Two notes for whoever picks this up:

- **The provider-less trap (#4514) is live on this screen.** The existing settings tests mount no `I18nProvider` and assert against raw text; `t()` outside a provider returns the key itself, which is exactly what `SettingsView.envelope.test.tsx` already pins for the hub (it asserts `console.settingsHub.empty` appears as literal text). Converting SettingsView's copy will need those tests updated in the same change, or they go red for the right reason in a confusing way.
- **#4579 deliberately did not fix this**, and added one more hardcoded string on purpose (`This deployment cannot encrypt secrets`, the new crypto-unavailable refusal). Routing one string through i18n would have left a single translated string among a dozen hardcoded ones in the same file and dragged ten locale packs into a card scoped to one view. It mirrors the surrounding convention instead, so this screen stays internally consistent and converts as one unit whenever this issue is picked up.

**PM ruling (delegated, veto window open):** one seat converts all of it as one unit — (a) the card's five originals: view-mode switcher labels, aggregate-footer prefixes keyed by aggregate KIND (`Avg`/`Sum`/`Min`/`Max`/`Count` all land, prefix from the bundle + number through the existing formatter), the form dialog's `sr-only` description fallback, and the dialog close button's `sr-only` label; (b) the SettingsView screen recorded in the comment below, including the save-bar counter through the i18n library's plural mechanism (never an English-only `(s)` rule) and #4579's deliberately-deferred crypto-refusal string. Rationale for absorbing (b): the comment's own analysis — the screen converts as one unit or the file stays internally split-conventioned.

Binding preconditions: the source thread objectstack#5084 MUST be read first — if any hold/restart condition there is still in force, STOP and report before editing. The #4514 provider-less trap is live on the settings tests — they update in the same change. All ten locale packs gain the new keys; `check:i18n-call-site-keys` + `check:i18n-en-drift` are the honesty gates.

Mutual exclusion: in-flight seats own `packages/types`+`core` type declarations (#4580), `scripts/**` (#4592), `packages/fields/**` (#4590), and `packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts` + dashboard docs/examples (#4356). This card touches none of those.

**PM step-7 复核: ACCEPT.** PR #4602 converts the whole unit exactly as ruled, and the census discipline paid for itself three times: (1) the source-thread precondition was honored and its '只补余量' instruction is what surfaced that the switcher was a pure WIRING gap (the bundle already carried all nine words — reused, so the picker and switcher cannot drift) and that the sr-only Close was objectstack#5505's remainder in the hand-written `custom/` wrapper its own fix couldn't reach; (2) the aggregate prefixes were found in plugin-grid's `useColumnSummary`, not plugin-list — why the original grep missed them; (3) SettingsView's true census was 18 literals, not 11. The plural work is the standard this repo wants: i18next native `_one/_other` WITH the base key (the #3863 ru fallback trap named and verified at counts 1/2/5), the two-sibling-key convention explicitly rejected with reasons, and the one wrong red-first prediction (en counter green pre-fix — the concatenation IS the English rule) recorded in the test header as the defect statement rather than quietly corrected. #4514 dispositions decided per-test by consumer (createSafeTranslation for published components, provider gained where interpolation is the assertion, envelope test deliberately provider-less with the why recorded). en-drift 0, ten packs purely additive, plugin-grid's .d.ts delta proven comment-only by strip-diff, changesets graded per package by position analysis. CI 20/20 zero failures.

Translation flags noted for a future native-speaker pass (ru/ar counter idioms, ko particle hedge, the deliberate fr space-colon) — none blocking.
